# QUMO

> QUMO is a fast, AI-native, hardware-neutral quantum software stack written in Mojo 1.1. It provides a flat circuit IR with affine symbolic parameters, OpenQASM 2/3 input and output, SIMD and multithreaded state-vector simulation, optional GPU acceleration through MAX (NVIDIA, AMD and Apple GPUs with the same kernels), stabilizer and Pauli-frame simulation, a vendor-neutral compiler (optimization, routing, basis translation), QEC (codes, detector error models, sparse-blossom MWPM, union-find and lookup decoders), and an algorithms library (VQE, QAOA, QPE, Grover, gradients). LLM agents use it through an MCP server and a JSON-speaking CLI. Python plugins run compiled circuits on quantum hardware (IBM Quantum, Quantinuum).

Conventions an agent must know:
- Circuits are exchanged as OpenQASM 3.0 text (2.0 is also accepted), for example: `OPENQASM 3.0; include "stdgates.inc"; qubit[2] q; bit[2] c; h q[0]; cx q[0], q[1]; c = measure q;`
- Qubit order is little-endian: bit k of a basis index is qubit k. Bitstrings are Qiskit-style: the leftmost character is the highest classical bit.
- Angles are in radians. `U(theta, phi, lambda)` follows OpenQASM 3, and `u3` is exactly `U`.
- Symbolic angles: declare `input float theta;` and use any expression affine in one input (`2*theta + pi/2`). Bind values with `params` as an array in declaration order or an object `{"theta": 0.1}`.
- Observables are Pauli sums such as `"0.5*Z0 Z1 - 1.2*X0 + 0.3"` or dense labels like `"ZZI"` (leftmost character = highest qubit).
- Results are deterministic: every random process takes a `seed` (default 1234).
- Errors look like `QM-Exxx: message (line L, col C). Hint: fix`. Codes are stable. Branch on the code and apply the hint. Warnings (`QM-Wxxx`) in tool results have the same JSON shape; QM-W020 means a requested GPU run fell back to the CPU; QM-W021 means a requested GPU precision did not apply (CPU simulators are fp64).
- QUMO-only operations (noise, detectors, observables) use `#pragma qumo ...` lines.

## Agent interfaces

- [AI-native interface design](docs/AI_NATIVE.md): OpenQASM subset, diagnostics, MCP tools, CLI, determinism, and how to register new tools and commands
- [Error and warning codes](docs/ERRORS.md): every QM-Exxx and QM-Wxxx code with its meaning and fix (generated from `error_catalog()`; includes the Python hardware-plugin range QM-E95x and benchmark-harness range QM-E96x)
- MCP server: run `build/qumo mcp` (MCP 2025-06-18, stdio). Tools: `qumo_run_qasm` (counts), `qumo_statevector`, `qumo_expectation`, `qumo_validate_qasm` (diagnostics and lint), `qumo_circuit_info` (depth, gate counts, T-count, flags), `qumo_convert` (canonical QASM 3, portable QASM 2 with `to: "qasm2"`, or circuit JSON), `qumo_describe` (gates, errors, capabilities; `format: "markdown"` for the error catalogue), `qumo_transpile` (vendor-neutral compile: target spec like `grid:4x4/sc_cz`, `trapped_ion:11`, or edges + basis), `qumo_estimate_resources` (logical, NISQ per modality, fault-tolerant), `qumo_vqe`, `qumo_qaoa_maxcut`, `qumo_qec_memory` (surface/repetition code logical error rate; decoders `mwpm` = sparse blossom (default), `sparse_blossom`, `mwpm_dense`, `uf`, `lookup`), `qumo_qec_dem` (Stim-format detector error model), `qumo_gpu_info` (is GPU support compiled in, which device, GPU precision and fp64 support), `qumo_run_device` (sample with `device` `auto`, `cpu` or `gpu` and `precision` `auto`, `fp32` or `fp64`; GPU state vectors run fp32 by default on every GPU, like CUDA-Q; `auto` = `QUMO_GPU_PRECISION` or the build default; fp64 on an Apple GPU is QM-E472; falls back to the CPU with warning QM-W020)
- Client config: `{"mcpServers":{"qumo":{"command":"/abs/path/QUMO/build/qumo","args":["mcp"]}}}`, or `claude mcp add qumo -- /abs/path/QUMO/build/qumo mcp`
- CLI: `qumo run|statevector|expect|validate|info|describe|convert|tool|mcp|version|help`. Add `--json` for machine output. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage. Build with `make cli` (CPU only) or `make cli-gpu` (`-D QUMO_GPU`, for NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm or Apple Metal). `qumo run x.qasm --device gpu --precision fp64` picks the device and the GPU precision.
- Hardware: `plugins/hardware` (Python package `qumo_hardware`) compiles with QUMO and submits to IBM Quantum or Quantinuum only after explicit confirmation (`--yes`); a `local` provider runs offline. See [Hardware plugins](docs/HARDWARE_PLUGINS.md).
- Self-description: `qumo describe gates|errors|capabilities --json` (generated from the implementation)

## Mojo API (compile with `-I .`)

- `qumo.ir.circuit`: `Circuit(n_qubits, n_clbits)` with methods `h x y z s t sx rx ry rz p u cx cz cp crx rzz swap ccx ...`, `measure(q, c)`, `measure_all()`, `reset`, `c_if(bit, val)`, `parameter(name)`, `bind(values)`, `inverse()`, `controlled(q)`, `power(k)`, `compose`, `depth()`, `t_count()`, `is_clifford()`, `validate()`
- `qumo.ir.gates`: opcodes `Op.*` and metadata (`op_name`, `op_arity`, `op_num_params`, `op_is_clifford`, `matrix_1q`, `matrix_2q`)
- `qumo.ir.qasm`: `parse_qasm(text) -> Circuit`, `parse_qasm_with_warnings(text, warnings)`, `load_qasm(path)`, `to_qasm(circuit) -> String` (OpenQASM 3)
- `qumo.ir.qasm2`: `to_qasm2(circuit) -> String`, portable OpenQASM 2 (original `qelib1.inc` plus exact gate definitions; loads in Qiskit strict and legacy modes, pytket and Cirq)
- `qumo.ir.pauli`: `parse_pauli_sum(text) -> PauliSum`
- `qumo.exec.dispatch`: `sample_auto(circuit, shots, seed)` picks Pauli-frame / tableau / CPU or GPU state vector automatically (reported in `.method`); `sample_on(circuit, shots, seed, params, device, note, precision="auto")` with device `auto`, `cpu` or `gpu` and GPU precision `auto`, `fp32` or `fp64`
- `qumo.gpu`: `query_gpu()`, `GpuStateVector` (fp32 by default on every GPU; fp64 on NVIDIA / AMD on request: `-D QUMO_GPU_FP64`, `QUMO_GPU_PRECISION=fp64` or `precision` arguments), `GpuFrameSampler` (build with `-D QUMO_GPU`; see [GPU](docs/GPU.md))
- `qumo.sim.runner`: `sample(circuit, shots, seed, params) -> SampleResult` (`.counts`, `.method`), `evolve(circuit, params) -> StateVector`, `expectation(circuit, H, params)`
- `qumo.sim.stabilizer`: `sample_stabilizer(circuit, shots, seed)` for Clifford circuits. `qumo.sim.frame` provides Pauli-frame batch sampling.
- `qumo.compiler.pass_manager`: `transpile(circuit, parse_target("grid:4x4"), level) -> CompileResult` (`.circuit`), `compile_spec(circuit, target, "pipeline text")`
- `qumo.qec`: `codes.surface_code_memory(d, rounds, NoiseParams)`, `codes.repetition_code_memory`, `codes.to_stim`, `dem.detector_error_model(circuit)`, `sparse_blossom.SparseBlossomDecoder` (default `mwpm`), `decoders.MwpmDecoder` (`mwpm_dense`) / `UnionFindDecoder` / `LookupTableDecoder`, `experiments.memory_experiment(code, d, rounds, p, shots, decoder)`
- `qumo.algorithms`: `library` (`ghz`, `qft`, `grover`, `qpe`, `trotter`), `variational` (`vqe`, `qaoa_maxcut`), `gradients.gradient`, `optimizers.minimize`, `hamiltonians` (`transverse_field_ising`, `heisenberg_xxz`, `h2_sto3g`, `ground_state`)
- `qumo.exec`: `primitives.run_sampler` / `run_estimator` (PUBs with parameter broadcasting), `orchestrator.Workflow` (HEFT over CPU/GPU/QPU pools), `resources.estimate_resources` / `estimate_hardware` / `estimate_fault_tolerant`
- Python: `build/qumo_py.so` (`make py`): `load_qasm`, `transpile(circ, n, edges, basis, level, seed)`, `sample`, `expectation`, benchmark generators
- `qumo.ai`: `json` (`JsonWriter`, `parse_json`), `diagnostics` (`Diagnostic`, `diagnostic_from_error`, `lint`, `error_catalog`), `describe` (`describe_*_json`, `circuit_to_json`, `circuit_from_json`, `circuit_summary_json`), `tools` (`ToolRegistry`, `default_registry`), `registry` (`full_registry` = core + module tools), `mcp` (`McpServer.handle`, `serve_stdio`)

## Examples

- [examples/bell.qasm](examples/bell.qasm): Bell pair
- [examples/ghz.qasm](examples/ghz.qasm): GHZ state built with a constant `for` loop
- [examples/teleport.qasm](examples/teleport.qasm): teleportation with mid-circuit measurement and feed-forward
- [examples/vqe_ansatz.qasm](examples/vqe_ansatz.qasm): parametric ansatz using `input float`
- [examples/bell_qasm2.qasm](examples/bell_qasm2.qasm): OpenQASM 2.0 input
- [examples/noisy_bell.qasm](examples/noisy_bell.qasm): `#pragma qumo` noise and a detector
